messages.author: 782ed6ec348dba9b
messages.subject: Updated data not accessed on Glimmer
parts:
Hi
  I have an app on glimmer which takes data from a csv. I have uploaded
a revised version of the csv containing updated info  and can see it in the file system but the app does not appear
to be reflecting the changes. Is there any obvious explanation for this?
http://glimmer.rstudio.com/pssguy/mlbPlayoffChances/

cheers
andrew clark

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: Updated data not accessed on Glimmer
parts:
Andrew,

You might need to refresh the app. The easiest way to do it is to add a restart.txt file to the root directory of your application and just touch it everytime you want the app to restart.

Hope this helps.

Best,
Ramnath

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: Updated data not accessed on Glimmer
parts:
Let me explain..

1. You need an empty `restart.txt` file per application, so put it in your mlbPlayoffChances folder.
2. Touching refers to just opening the file and saving it so that the time stamp changes. You can do it in unix using touch restart.txt, hence the name

Best,
Ramnath

messages.subject: Re: Updated data not accessed on Glimmer
parts:
I would recommend putting system("touch restart.txt") inside of your shinyServer function, if anything. Otherwise, your app will restart over and over as the browser makes many requests to load all the page assets.

In the future we'll have reactive versions of the file reading functions, so this should be taken care of automatically (not even a browser reload necessary, I'd imagine).

messages.subject: Re: Updated data not accessed on Glimmer
parts:
Andrew, I have a similar issue with reactiveFileReader, and I hope it's ok if I post it here, so perhaps people that replied to you before will see this as well. Besides, you could see how it can be used more or less successfully.

Here's my code for server.R file for a Shiny app, notice that hours is now a function that you will refer to as hours() further.

#server.R
require(rCharts)
shinyServer(
  function(input, output, session) {
       hours <- reactiveFileReader(1000, session, 'data/hours.csv', read.csv)
          output$chart1 <- renderChart({
          HoursPlot <- hPlot(x="Manager", y="HoursLogged", type="bar", data=hours(), title = "Hours Logged This Month")
          HoursPlot$yAxis(title = list(text = "Hours Logged")) 
          HoursPlot$addParams(height = 600, dom = 'chart1')
          return(HoursPlot)
          })
        
  }
)

According to the manual of reactiveFileReader this placement of the function inside shinyServer() will make it work per-session, and it actually works great inside RStudio (I have Windows): every time I make changes to the hours.csv file in data folder, it instantly updates the chart in RStudio. However, once deployed on Shinyapps.io it only shows static data (what was originally in hours.csv), it doesn't seem to update reactively as it should. I know if I re-deploy the app, the data will be refreshed, but what's the point of reactiveFileReader() then? I would really like for it to work properly, and if I place this function outside of shinyServer() (above the call), it will load for a second and shut down, which is not acceptable obviously.

Please advise. Thank you!

On Friday, 24 May 2013 09:40:09 UTC-7, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:


I would recommend putting system("touch restart.txt") inside of your shinyServer function, if anything. Otherwise, your app will restart over and over as the browser makes many requests to load all the page assets.

In the future we'll have reactive versions of the file reading functions, so this should be taken care of automatically (not even a browser reload necessary, I'd imagine).

Let me explain..

1. You need an empty `restart.txt` file per application, so put it in your mlbPlayoffChances folder.
2. Touching refers to just opening the file and saving it so that the time stamp changes. You can do it in unix using touch restart.txt, hence the name
